FROM ONE LINE TO TWO

A familiar melody.
A different way to listen.

Counterline learns a first part, then helps you explore what happens when another voice joins it.

01

Give it a cantus.

Tap Record cantus, sing a short phrase on its own, then tap Finish & save. Or import an audio file. Listen back to check the melody it learned.

02

Add your voice.

Choose Solo practice, connect headphones, and tap Start practice. The recording plays while the app listens to your second line. Loop it as often as you like.

03

Explore the interval.

Watch the live interval and its tuning in cents. Choose pure ratios or equal temperament. Adjust smoothing and jump confirmation to find a comfortable response.

FOR YOUR OWN PRACTICE

A duet, even on your own.

The recorded cantus provides the reference; the microphone follows you. Wired headphones give the clearest separation and most predictable timing. You can save several cantus recordings locally and export WAV files to share with a student.

Practice a second line ↗
FOR TWO LIVE CHOIR PARTS

Let the melody lead.

In Live choir, both parts sing into the phone. The learned cantus guides the tracker, while both pitches are measured live. Start together at the beginning of the learned phrase, and use Restart learned phrase if the follower loses its place.

Experimental · best with short, sustained phrases
READY FOR YOUR MUSIC STAND

Keep it on your
Android home screen.

No app store needed. Start in Chrome.

Open Counterline ↗
  1. 1
    Open the practice room.

    Use the Open Counterline button on your Android phone. Allow microphone access when you record or practice.

  2. 2
    Add it to your home screen.

    In Chrome, tap the ⋮ menu, then Add to Home screen or Install app. The wording depends on your browser.

  3. 3
    Keep the screen open while singing.

    The app stops listening in the background. After its first complete load, the practice room can work offline. Recordings are stored in this browser on this device.

A practice companion, still finding its voice.

This is an experimental prototype. Headphone practice uses a single live voice and is the best place to start. Two-part microphone tracking can struggle with unisons, octaves, quiet voices, or reverberant rooms. An uncertain reading is shown as uncertain. Test it with your singers before relying on fine tuning measurements.

Recordings stay on your device; they are never uploaded. Clearing browser data removes them, and another browser or website address has its own library. Export important recordings as WAV files. Recording and import are limited to two minutes per phrase.
